rules.message: force push rewrites shared history; push a new commit or ask the operator
--no-verify skips the hooks; fix the finding instead
git commit -n skips the hooks; fix the finding instead
push to a protected branch; push a feature branch and open a pull request
gh api with a mutating method; use a read-only call, ops/conductor/gh_ops.py or ask the operator
gh api with fields sends POST unless its own tokens say exactly -X GET (or --method GET); use a read-only call, ops/conductor/gh_ops.py or ask the operator
GitHub writes go through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py; read-only gh subcommands (list, view) stay allowed

rules.pattern: ^gh(?!\s+(?:api|status|search|browse|help|version|--version|--help|-h|completion|auth status|pr (?:list|view|diff|checks|status|checkout)|issue (?:list|view|status)|run (?:list|view|watch|download)|workflow (?:list|view|run proof\.yml)|release (?:list|view|download)|repo (?:view|clone|list)|label list|cache list|variable (?:list|get)|secret list|ruleset (?:list|view|check)|gist (?:list|view)|project (?:list|view|item-list|field-list)|extension list|alias list|config (?:get|list)|org list)(?:\s|$))(?:\s|$)
rules.message: only read-only gh subcommands (list, view, status, checks, gh api reads, gh workflow run proof.yml) run from a session; every GitHub write, gh auth token, gh alias and gh extension go through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py or the operator
a write to the GitHub API outside gh_ops.py; use ops/conductor/gh_ops.py or ask the operator
a git alias can run any program behind a harmless name; run the command directly
git -c alias.* can run any program behind a harmless name; run the command directly
CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE starts claude without the project hooks and settings; run claude with the project settings
a script fed to a shell by redirect or process substitution is hidden from the guard; run the script file directly
git configuration from the environment can define aliases and hooks the guard cannot see; run git as it is
git filter-branch and filter-repo run arbitrary programs over the history; ask the operator
call gh by its name so the gh rules can read the command
pushing every ref can overwrite or delete protected branches; push one feature branch
--admin bypasses branch protection; wait for the required checks and reviews
changing core.hooksPath switches the git hooks off; ask the operator
git -c core.hooksPath switches the git hooks off; ask the operator
a command piped or fed into a shell is hidden from the guard; run the command directly
re-baselining, anchoring and syncing the controls is the operator's step; deliver a patch and ask
moving or removing the reference the gates compare against is the operator's step; ask
hiding changes from git hides them from the gates; ask the operator
piping a download into a shell runs unreviewed code; download, read, then run
GATES_OFFLINE turns missing tools into skips; run the gates as they are
a token with a known vendor prefix ends up in logs; read it from the environment
a secret literal in a command ends up in logs; read it from the environment
bypassing the permission checks (or loading settings other than .claude/settings.json) switches deny rules off; run claude with the project settings
a release runs only through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py dispatch-release; the only workflow a session may name directly is gh workflow run proof.yml, and gh_ops.py dispatch-proof is preferred
pushing a tag starts a release; the release goes through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py dispatch-release only
push.followTags pushes tags with every push; the release goes through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py dispatch-release only
fetching into a remote-tracking ref moves the reference the gates compare against; plain git fetch only
git -c remote.* rewires where fetch writes or reads; plain git fetch only
a local branch or tag named origin/... shadows the remote-tracking ref the gates and worktrees start from; pick another name

write_rules.message: a secret literal must not be written into a file; read it from the environment or a secret store
a token with a known vendor prefix must not be written into a file
a private key must not be written into a file
